该固件可快速体验Blynk同时通过串口通讯让任意单片机接入Blynk，利用固件板: This firmware can quickly experience Blynk and allow any microcontroller to access Blynk through serial communication. Using the onboard function of the firmware, you can also directly use Blynk to control the ATOM pin level status and obtain pin level changes. It can easily convert the sensor into an IoT remote sensor or actuator, making the use of the IoT more convenient. Simple, press and hold the onboard button for the first time without releasing it, click the reset button, release it when the indicator light flashes red and blue alternately, the device automatically turns on the hotspot ATOM_Blynk_XXXXXXXXX, password XXXXXXXX, connect to this hotspot to access the IP address 192.168.4.1 to access the configuration server and network After confirming that the network information is correct, restart the device and start using it. The device is disconnected from the Blynk server. The indicator light continues to flash with a cycle of 100 milliseconds. The baud rate of the hardware serial port and the soft serial port are both 9600, of which the soft serial port RX (26) TX (32), the serial port passes the jso of ["PIN", "value"] n format data interactive virtual pin data, for example ["V6", "1"] means that virtual pin V6 has sent or received data 1, V0-V7 has been occupied by ATOM. Please use other virtual pins for other purposes. The example server address is the domestic free Blynk server address for testing only. Please deploy the server privately for stable use. Warm reminder: When connecting to a computer for the first time, open the serial port monitor with a baud rate of 9600 and check the debugging information.

「オルゴール工房」\n手作り手回しオルゴールを楽しめるアプリです。\n手回しオル:
"Music box workshop"
This is an app where you can enjoy handmade hand-cranked music boxes.
You can enjoy the feeling of punching holes in the paper of a hand-cranked music box and playing it.
In real life, you would need many sheets of paper, but with this app, even if you make a mistake, you can correct it and try again as many times as you like.
You can write your own songs on the music box board and give them as gifts, or you can import them to your smartphone using a QR code.

Main features
- Song data can be transferred to the board and played on the board
- Can input from quarter note to 64th note
・256 steps for quarter notes, 4096 steps for 64th notes
- Possible to set tempo during playback
・2 octave keyboard input
・Simultaneous pronunciation of up to 3 notes per step
・Up to 250 sounds can be input
・Save data (automatically load when restarting the app)
・You can exchange composition data with your smartphone via QR code.
・Can save and read from SD card
・You can delete the input sound by reselecting it.
- Automatically scrolls as you type (when scrolling is on)
・Screen up/down scroll key (long press to fast forward)
-You can set the end position of the song using the END button.
・One line insertion and one line deletion function
・You can transfer the song data you created to the Frisk-sized music box workshop board and play it on the board.

How to use
●Top screen
When you press a key, that note will sound and a mark will be added.
The scroll will advance one note according to the set note (quarter note to 64th note).
Notes can be changed using the "↑" and "↓" buttons on the right.
You can move the editing position using the "↑" and "↓" buttons on the left, and the sound at the moved position will be played.
Press and hold the "↑" and "↓" buttons to fast forward. At this time, no sound will be played.
When you press the "Save" button, it will be saved to the device and automatically loaded the next time it is started.
To listen to the song you typed from the beginning, press the "Start" button to move to the beginning of the song, then press the "Play" button.
The performance will stop automatically when it reaches the end of the song.
If you want to stop midway through, press the "Play" button.
When you press the "Insert" button, one line (the length of the current note) is inserted at the current editing position.
Press the "Delete" button to delete one line at the current editing position.
Press the "Settings" button to display the settings menu screen.

●Settings menu screen
Pressing the "Delete All" button twice will clear all composition data.
If you press the "Free Performance" button to turn it on, you can enjoy playing freely without recording.
You can save data to the SD card using the "SD Save" button.
The file name to be saved can be an 8-digit number.
You can read song data saved on the SD card using the "SD Read" button.
Song data is limited to 100 songs.
If you turn on the "Auto Scroll" button, it will automatically scroll by one note when you press a key.
You can adjust the volume with the "Volume" button.
You can change the tempo with the "Tempo" button. (30-240)
When you press the "QR display" button, the current song data will be converted into a QR code and displayed.
You can transfer the composition data to the Music Box Studio board using the "Transfer" button.
It can be loaded using the smartphone app "Music Box Workshop".

●Transfer created song data to the board
You can transfer song data created to the music box workshop board and play it on the board.
Press the "Transfer" button on the menu to display the song data transfer screen.
Press and hold the button on the board to make the LED blink slowly (write mode).
Place the board so that the light sensor is directly above the light emitting part and press the "Transfer" button.
During writing, the LED on the board changes from flashing to lit, and the progress bar advances.
When data writing is successful, the LED on the board turns off.
If data transfer fails, the LED on the board will flash rapidly, so press the button on the board (to cancel write mode) and try again.

For videos on how to use it, please search for "Music Box Workshop" and "Writing song data to electronic music box board using smartphone app" on YouTube.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gKYO2o_FNh4
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EFtbN6PRWyo
The board is on sale at Mercari and Switch Science. Please search for "Music box workshop".

Client: M5Core2 with Audio Module (M144)

Server: Raspberry Pi Zero 2W

Transceivers: Yaesu FT‑991A / Icom IC‑705

Hardware Extensions
PTT via Port B (Mechanical Key + SK6812):
A mechanical key connected to Port B can now trigger PTT.

Rotary Encoder on Port A (SKU: U135):
A rotary encoder connected to Port A can be used to operate the main screen controls.

Audio Reception via Module Audio (SKU: M144):
The system can receive audio from the transceiver through the M144 audio module.

Raspberry Pi Zero 2W Setup

Firmware version v1.04
Turn the M5StickS3 into a physical remote control for WorkBuddy. Bluetooth direct connection (sticks3-ctl), no driver installation required, no USB port occupied.


【Hold method】
In order to hold the phone stably, you need to hold it the other way around (buttons facing down), and the screen has been rotated 180° to accommodate this position.

【button】

· Press and hold the front button - voice recording (press and hold to record, release to end)

· Front key click - send message (Enter)



· Front key double-click - open/hide the left column (Cmd+B)

· Front key triple-click - control the right column (Shift+Cmd+B)


· Side key click - Stop generation (Esc)

· Press and hold the side button - clear all input text



· Left flick - next task (Cmd+])

· Right Swipe - Previous Task (Cmd+[)


Shaking does not require pressing buttons, just shake directly; shaking will be ignored during recording, and the column will not be cut if the hand shakes when speaking.

【Screen】
Displays the current task name and running status (generating/idle/completed), which will automatically change after task switching.
The screen will automatically turn off after 30 seconds of no operation, and will light up if you raise your hand or press a button; the WorkBuddy icon and zs will pop up one after another 5 seconds before the screen turns off.
MAC is displayed in the upper right corner, indicating that the modifier key (Cmd) of macOS is currently being pressed to send.

【sound】
The buttons have differentiated short beeps and a beep when a task is completed, so you don’t have to stare at the screen all the time.

[Prerequisites for use]
1. The key bindings are aligned with the WorkBuddy default shortcut keys. If you have changed the shortcut keys, you need to change the firmware config.h and recompile.
2. The task name on the screen requires the computer (macOS) to run the supporting status bridge, read the local task status and push it to the device via Bluetooth. When the bridge is not running, the keyboard is fully functional and the screen only displays "Waiting for synchronization".
3. For first time use, pair StickS3-Ctl in System Settings → Bluetooth.

【Burning】
Merged image (including bootloader + partition table + application), Flash address 0x0.

Based on Arduino + M5Unified + NimBLE, 8-byte standard 6KRO keyboard report, compatible with macOS boot protocol analysis.

AirSerial turns PowerHub into a WiFi wireless serial port bridge, remote burning/debugging ESP32/ESP8266:


● Dual Host ports on the front (Type-A + Type-C) automatically switch: the target board can be used wherever it is plugged in, and it will automatically recognize and reconnect in about 5 seconds

● esptool Standard handshake: rfc2217://:3334, automatically reset to download mode without pressing keys

● Web Portal: network configuration, USB Host switch, status monitoring, WebSocket terminal + !airsn local command

● Transparent TCP (3333) + RFC2217 (3334) dual port, pyserial can be used directly as a local serial port

● WS2812 status light: WiFi status, power/charging (orange breathing), device heartbeat, USB routing indication, red flashing alarm for backflow

● Backflow protection: Automatically cut off the front port power supply when detecting external 5V backflow

● Report unexpected restart reasons (WDT/panic classification)


First use: Bottom Type-C is connected to the computer for burning, open http://192.168.4.1/ Configure the network, switch the device to STA and go online, turn on the USB Host switch on the web page, plug the target board into the front port and use it.

CAM VIEW - M5 Cardputer Camera Viewer Firmware v2.0
================================================================
Applicable hardware: M5Stack Cardputer ADV (ESP32-S3 / 8MB Flash / 240x135 screen)
Supporting software: PC "Camera LAN Live Broadcast" package (another compressed package)
================================================================


[1. What is this]

Turn Cardputer into a portable monitor:
Turn on the computer and connect to WiFi → type the IP address of the computer with the keyboard → the screen will directly display the image of the computer camera.

It looks at the MJPEG stream on port 8090 on the computer:
480x270 JPEG, 10 fps, ~7 KB per frame, ~0.3 sec latency

The mobile phone/tablet side is not affected. You can still scan the QR code to view the web page on port 8889. Both channels work at the same time.


[2. Load the firmware (only once)]

The compiled entire firmware has been included in the package: firmware\camview-v2.0-8MB.bin
Choose one of the following three methods. Method A is recommended.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
Method A: Burning with graphic tools (easiest)
─────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Download Espressif’s official tool ESP32 Flash Download Tool
(Search "flash_download_tool", official website dl.espressif.com
Or it’s also available in the releases of GitHub espressif/esptool)
2. Open the tool → ChipType and select ESP32-S3 → WorkMode and select Develop → OK
3. Fill in the following:
File: firmware\camview-v2.0-8MB.bin
Address: 0x0 (note it is 0x0, not 0x1000)
勾选那一行的复选框\n SPI SPEED：80MHz:
Check the box for that row
       SPI SPEED：80MHz
       SPI MODE ：DIO
       FLASH SIZE：8MB
4. Select the COM port (it will appear after the device is connected to USB-C, driver-free for Windows 10/11)
5. Click START and wait for the progress bar to finish (about 40 seconds). When FINISH appears, it is successful.
6. Unplug the USB and power on again

─────────────────────────────────────────────
Method B: Command line (if esptool is installed)
─────────────────────────────────────────────
  esptool.exe --chip esp32s3 -p COM3 -b 460800 write_flash 0x0 camview-v2.0-8MB.bin

Replace COM3 with your actual serial port number. You can see it in Device Manager → Ports on Windows.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
Method C: Source code compilation (if you want to change it yourself)
─────────────────────────────────────────────
The source code is in the source\camview\ directory. Use Arduino IDE to open camview.ino.

Dependent libraries (versions must be consistent, otherwise they may not be compiled):
    M5Cardputer    1.1.1
    M5Unified      0.2.29
    M5GFX          0.2.36
    JPEGDEC        1.8.5
    esp32 core     3.3.12
qrcodegen comes with the source code (qrcodegen.c / qrcodegen.h, no need to install it separately)

arduino-cli installation dependencies:
    arduino-cli lib install "M5Cardputer@1.1.1"
    arduino-cli lib install "JPEGDEC@1.8.5"
    arduino-cli core install esp32:esp32@3.3.12

Development board settings (must be consistent, otherwise there is not enough memory):
开发板 ESP32S3 Dev Module\n Fla:
Development board ESP32S3 Dev Module
    Flash Size  8MB (64Mb)
Partition plan Huge APP (3MB No OTA/1MB SPIFFS)
USB CDC On Boot Default (firmware does not rely on serial port output)

After compilation and uploading, it takes up about 37% of Flash.


[3. First time use: equipped with WiFi (only once)]

1. After booting, the screen displays "Setup Mode", indicating that the network has not been configured yet.
2. Use your mobile phone to connect to a WiFi called Cardputer-Cam (no password, there is also a QR code on the screen)
3. Open http://192.168.4.1 in the mobile browser
4. Fill in your home WiFi name and password → Save, the device will automatically restart
5. Automatically connect to the Internet after restarting and enter the address input interface.


[4. Daily use]

When "Enter PC address" appears on the screen:

1. Use the keyboard to enter the computer’s IP, for example 192.168.1.100
· No need to enter the port, the firmware will automatically fill in 8090
· What you lost last time will be automatically remembered and will be brought out next time you start the game.
2. Press Enter → Display Connecting → The screen will appear after about 2 seconds
The green number in the upper right corner is the real-time frame rate (stable 10 fps)
3. Press Esc to exit the screen and return to the input interface

Keystroke quick check (input interface)
Enter to start watching
Del backspace
Esc Clear and re-enter
Ctrl+Del Restore factory settings (clear WiFi and addresses, reset everything)

Keystroke quick check (viewing interface)
Esc to exit viewing
C Switch color mode (used when the picture has a color cast, the settings will be remembered)

The screen will automatically turn off if you don't touch the keyboard for 90 seconds, and light up if you press any key. Do not turn off the screen when watching the picture.


[5. Disconnection and self-healing]

· Turn off push streaming on the computer: reconnect #n is displayed in the upper right corner and keeps retrying.
· Re-push the stream on the computer: the screen will be automatically restored within about 3 seconds without restarting the device.
· 10 consecutive failures: Automatically reconnect to WiFi
· 40 consecutive failures: the whole machine automatically restarts (you can save yourself even if it is stuck)


【6. Frequently Asked Questions】

Q The color of the screen is wrong (blurred screen, color cast, purple color)
A Press the C key to switch the color mode. Press it once to view it and it will be remembered automatically.
Normally, the machine is correct when it leaves the factory and is generally not used.
Q 一直 Connecting 或显示 no stream\nA ① 电脑端:
Q keeps Connecting or shows no stream
A ① The push stream on the computer is not enabled: double-click "Start push stream.vbs"
② The IP is entered incorrectly: refer to the address in the pop-up window on the computer.
③ The computer and Cardputer are not in the same WiFi

Q There is a picture but it is frozen, and the frame rate is always 0
A Click any key on the keyboard to wake it up (the screen may be off).
If that still doesn't work, press Esc to exit and Enter to re-enter.

Q Changed WiFi password/replaced router
A Press Ctrl+Del on the input interface to restore factory settings and re-use the third part of the distribution network.

Q There are black edges on the screen/the proportion is wrong
A Normal. A 480x270 stream is scaled down to 240x135 with minimal difference.

Q How long can I watch?
A Just leave it on all the time, the power consumption is very low. Does not sleep when powered by USB (except screen).


[7. Technical Parameters]

Main control ESP32-S3 (M5Stack Cardputer ADV)
Screen 240x135 ST7789
Firmware framework Arduino + M5Cardputer 1.1.1 + JPEGDEC 1.8.5
Video source PC ffmpeg extracts frames from the live stream → 480x270 JPEG
Decoding Hardware-level JPEG decoding → write directly to screen, RGB565
Frame rate: stable 10 frames/second (speed limit on computer)
Delay approximately 0.3 seconds
Bandwidth approximately 70 KB/s
Storage WiFi and address are stored in NVS and will not be lost when power is off.

# CoreInk Humidor & Environmental Monitor - v1.0.0 Release Package

---
[firmware name]
CoreInk Humidor & Environmental Monitor (cigar humidor / indoor environment monitor)

[Required external hardware/sensor instructions]
⚠️ The following sensors must be connected to run this firmware, otherwise environment sensing cannot be completed:
• Main control device: M5Stack CoreInk (ESP32-PICO-D4, 1.54-inch E-Ink electronic ink screen)
• Required sensor: M5Stack Unit ENV-Pro (built-in Bosch BME688 sensor, SKU: U170)
• Connection method: Directly plug into Port A on the top of the CoreInk body through the Grove HY2.0-4P cable (I2C port: SDA=G32, SCL=G33)

【Main features】
1. The ink screen has full positive phase black text display on a white background, eye-friendly paper texture, clear strong light, and dual-batch screen (D67/M09) dynamic drive to prevent freezing.
2. Full-dimensional monitoring of indoor and cigar maintenance: high-precision temperature and humidity (0.1 resolution/65% golden reference line), air pressure, converted altitude, Bosch BSEC air quality (IAQ/Static IAQ/bVOC/eCO2) and gas-sensitive resistor native resistance.
3. Hyperbolic historical trend line chart: supports 10m / 1h / 6h / 24h / 2d / 7d scroll wheel free zoom and historical translation backtracking.
4. Four-level intelligent power consumption architecture: Realtime (high-frequency monitoring ~10h), Balanced (daily light sleep ~6 days), Eco ULP (10-minute cycle deep sleep ~2 months), On-Demand (on-demand wake-up measurement ~4 months+).
5. Wi-Fi NTP can be selected to adjust the time to the hardware RTC when it is turned on. After the time adjustment is completed, the Wi-Fi radio frequency is completely disconnected, resulting in pure offline zero radiation and long battery life.

【Key operation】
• G5 (EXT button): Short press to switch between [Main Dashboard] and [Air Quality Laboratory]; long press (>=800ms) to call out [Power Consumption Mode Menu].
• Three-way trackwheel on the top: G37 (push up to zoom in/backward), G39 (pull down to zoom out/pan forward), G38 (short press on the middle button to switch zoom/pan mode).
• Power button (G27): Click to restart; double-click to shut down completely.

# DeskClock for Cardputer ADV

Cardputer ADV desktop information panel program based on `UIFlow2/MicroPython`.

## Project Introduction

This program runs on `Cardputer ADV` and is used to display information such as time, date, weather, sunrise and sunset, longitude and latitude, Maidenhead grid and current call sign on the main interface.

The current version prioritizes "stable and usable" and is suitable as a basic version for daily maintenance and subsequent upgrades.

## Main functions

- Local time display, according to East Eighth District school time
- UTC time display
- Date and day display
- Pull real weather data by latitude and longitude
- Display real-time temperature
- Pull the real sunrise and sunset times after connecting to the Internet
- Display the currently used latitude and longitude
- Calculate 6-digit Maidenhead grid based on latitude and longitude
- Display the call sign currently being contacted via WS
- Support WiFi automatic connection, scanning, and saving
- Support setting fixed city, fixed latitude and longitude, GPS switch, WS server IP
-Support brightness switching, screen off, and battery check
-Support manual refresh of weather and WS

## Main interface display content

- local time
- UTC time
- date
- Week
- status bar
- temperature
-Current call sign
- Maidenhead 6-bit grid
- Latitude / Longitude
- Sunrise / Sunset

## Key description

Under the main interface:

- `L`: switch brightness, 4 levels in total
  - `100%`
  - `75%`
  - `50%`
  - `25%`
- `ESC`: turn off the screen, press it again to turn on the screen
- `S`: Enter the settings page
- `B`: Display the current battery level
- `R`: Refresh weather, temperature, sunrise, sunset
- `W`: Reconnect to WS and refresh call sign data

Under the settings interface:

- `;`: Move selection up
- `.`: Move selection down
- `Enter`: enter or edit the current item
- `ESC`: Return to the main interface

## Setting page

Current settings include:

- `City`
- `Lat`
- `Lon`
- `GPS`
- `IP`
- `WiFi Setup`
- `Back`

illustrate:

- When `GPS = OFF`, the weather is pulled based on the filled in fixed longitude and latitude
- When `GPS = ON`, priority is given to using the longitude and latitude obtained by GPS
- `IP` is used to connect to the callsign WS service

## WiFi logic

After booting, the program will first try to connect to the saved WiFi.
If the saved WiFi is not available, you can enter `WiFi Setup`:

1. Scan surrounding WiFi
2. Select network
3. Enter password
4. Connect and save

## Weather and location logic

Weather, temperature, sunrise, and sunset are all pulled according to the "currently used longitude and latitude":

- GPS off: Use `Lat / Lon` filled in settings
- GPS on: Prioritize using GPS coordinates

The Maidenhead grid is also calculated in real time at the currently used latitude and longitude.

## Call sign display logic

The `Call:` area of ​​the main interface is used to display the call sign currently being contacted.

- When the WS connection is successful, the status can be displayed as `WS OK`
- Display `WS Off` when not connected
- `WS Try` can be displayed during reconnection process

In the current version, the call sign font color has been set to red.

## Common meanings of status bar

- `Boot`: starting
- `Clock OK`: Time adjustment successful
- `Clock Loc`: use local time
- `Wx OK`: Weather refreshed successfully
- `Wx Off`: Weather refresh failed
- `WS OK`: WS is connected
- `WS Off`: WS is not connected
- `WS Try`: WS heavy
- `Offline`: The network is not connected
- `BATxx%`: current battery capacity
- `BL 100% / 75% / 50% / 25%`: brightness level

Commonly used keys
· Press and hold Enter: speak, release to send
· Y / N / A: Execute / Cancel / This task will be executed subsequently
· ; and .: move up and down the timeline; / open details;, return to the latest
· `(Esc): Cancel the current task
· Btn0: Switch Agent/SSH
· Fn+W: Settings (Wi-Fi, Key, SSH host, mobile phone scan code settings)
· Fn+H: Help
· Fn+Del: Clear conversation memory

Note: Only Cardputer Adv is supported. The firmware does not contain any Key. esptool.py --chip esp32s3 write_flash 0x0 GeminiPuter.bin

13 种角色、11 种颜色、12 种随机轮换表情的独立离线演示。触摸控制头部和视:
Independent offline demo of 13 characters, 11 colors, and 12 randomly rotating expressions. Touch controls the head and line of sight, and the IMU supports relative posture following, no network or account required.

## operate
- Left A click: Switch characters (~320 ms delay to differentiate between double clicks).
- Right B-click: Toggle colors.
- Double-click A: Set the current posture to the IMU neutral position, and stay still for a moment during the prompt.
- Press and hold A+B simultaneously for one second: recalibration is also possible.
- Touch or drag: Head and eyes follow the finger, touch takes precedence over the IMU.

## 0.3.0
The character stands upright when running, and is obviously elongated and squashed when closed; the heart-shaped bottom is rounder, and the four-pointed star notch is shallower. The triangular character adopts a conical surface, and the eyes rotate along the curved surface and are naturally blocked on the sides. The IMU combines gyroscope and gravity direction to support left and right rotation when held vertically. The relative heading may drift slowly, you can double-click A to reset it to zero.

466×466 native resolution, contour drawing and partial refresh. 0.3.0 has been burned on a white TriviaPOD TP-01-A (32 MB Flash / 8 MB PSRAM) and fully read back for verification. The default water drop face stable phase is about 27–30 FPS, with a median of 29.8 FPS. The frame rate of other characters has not been measured one by one; the physical IMU following direction and feel still need to be confirmed by trials. StopWatch C152 uses the same board-level driver, and this round has not been verified on the actual C152.

This is a pure expression demonstration, speaking and listening are animated states, and does not include speech recognition, TTS or networking functions. After restarting, the characters and colors return to their default values.

Burn merged BIN to **0x0**. The image uses a 16 MB Flash layout and will replace the boot, partition, configuration and application within the coverage. Please back up the original firmware and configuration that need to be retained first.

v7.5 - 2026-10-02\nPackage Manager (Tool:
v7.5 - 2026-10-02
Package Manager (Tools -> Package Manager)
New item Tools -> Package Manager (file main/apps/tools/package_manager.cpp): installing packages via WiFi directly from the device. Three sections:
Games - games from the apps_k85os repository (release with the app tag).
Themes - UEFI/BIOS themes .thm from apps_k85os/uefi. Already downloaded ones are marked [installed] and are applied via BIOS -> Update UEFI theme.
Firmware - firmware from the latest k85OS release (.bin list + signature).
Games and firmware are written to a free OTA slot with confirmation. Ed25519 signature required: packages without signature are rejected. The name of the installed package is remembered only after successful firmware installation.
Launch the installed image: BIOS -> System tools -> Slots & partitions -> Boot other slot.
Themes are downloaded through a temporary file with size and name checking (protection against download interruption and path substitution). Package lists are stored in PSRAM rather than static RAM.
Scripts, scheduler, FTP
Автозапуск: /littlefs/startup.sh выполня:
Autostart: /littlefs/startup.sh is executed at boot. All shell commands and new ones are supported: echo, set NAME=value (variables $NAME, built-in $IP, $SSID), alias / unalias, sleep N, sh file, exit, reboot, # comments.
Scheduler (cron): file /littlefs/crontab, format min hour day month weekday command (*, */N, ranges, lists). Execution log in /littlefs/cron.log. The tasks run after time synchronization via NTP. Cron command on|off|reload|list.
FTP server: Tools -> FTP Server (also Tools -> Services). Copy PC <-> device files (download, upload, delete, rename, folders). Root /littlefs, STA network only (not accessible via hotspot), passive mode, one client. The login is specified by the ftppass <user> <password> command in Terminal/SSH, the password is stored as a hash. The download goes to a temporary file, auto-shutdown after 15 minutes without clients, autostart is enabled in Services.
Services дополнен пунктами FTP Server, F:
Services is supplemented with FTP Server, FTP autostart, Startup script, Scheduler (cron) items.

产品简介\n\nM5 INTEL 是为 M5StickS3 开发的离线近距离情报:
Product introduction

M5 INTEL is an offline NFC firmware developed for the M5StickS3. Devices communicate directly via ESP-NOW, without relying on a phone, computer, Wi-Fi router or the internet. It integrates temporary voices, preset short messages, status codes, digital intelligence, device telemetry, IMU hand signals, timing beacons and SOS alarms into a vertical screen cyber terminal interface.

Current version number: v1.0.0
Target hardware: M5StickS3/ESP32-S3-PICO-1/8 MB Flash
Communication method: ESP-NOW, direct communication with devices on the same channel
Firmware type: Complete merged image, burned from 0x00000000

### Main functions

1. M5 TALK
- Record voice using built-in microphone.
- The maximum recording time is 8 seconds.
- The screen displays the recording duration in real time.
- After the recording is completed, it can be reliably sent to the device on the same channel.
- The receiving end displays the sender and voice duration through a global pop-up window.
- BtnB plays the voice, BtnA confirms and destroys it from memory.

2. QUICK INTEL
   - SAFE
   - NEED SUPPORT
   - TARGET FOUND
   - RETREAT
   - RENDEZVOUS
   - MISSION COMPLETE

3. STATUS CODE
   - GREEN
   - AMBER
   - RED
   - HOLD
   - MOVING
   - OFFLINE

4. NUMERIC INTEL
- Supports sending digital intelligence from 00–99.
- Can be used for number of people, target, distance, room or task number.

5. TELEMETRY
- Send the battery percentage of the device.
- Send the device boot time.

6. IMU SIGNAL
- Send hand signals by visibly shaking the device.
- Approximately 2.5g trigger threshold.
- 15 seconds cooldown to avoid repeated triggering.
- Pause detection during recording.

7. BEACON
- Send online status and battery level every 30 seconds.
- Only sent when a device on the same channel is found and is not recording.
- Runs in the background without popping up interfering windows.

8. SOS
- Send high priority emergency alerts.
- The receiving end displays a separate red SOS page.
- Play a short beep once.
- BtnB acknowledges and disarms the alert.

### UI and message experience
- Matrix 风格绿色数字雨启动动画。\n- 像素赛博风 M5 INTEL:
- Matrix style green digital rain start animation.
- Pixel cyber style M5 INTEL Logo.
- Black background, green message, red alert.
- All functions adopt vertical screen layout.
- Off-screen double-buffered drawing to reduce screen flickering.
- Display current channel and number of online devices.
- Ordinary messages and voices can be received on any function page.
- Messages are displayed in a global pop-up window, and long content is automatically divided into lines.
- After closing the pop-up window, return to the page you were on before receiving.
- Timing beacons do not pop up and do not interrupt operations.

### Reliable transmission

- Voice is downsampled and then transmitted in fragments.
- The data packet contains message ID, fragment sequence number, total number of fragments, duration and CRC16.
- The receiving end returns ACK piece by piece.
- The sender only resends missing fragments and performs up to 5 rounds of selective retransmission.
- Default messages, status, digital, telemetry, IMU and SOS also await confirmation of receipt.
- DELIVERED means the peer has acknowledged it.
- NOT CONFIRMED means complete confirmation was not obtained and needs to be retried.
- Automatic deduplication of duplicate messages and clearing of incomplete voice messages after timeout.

### How to operate

Main menu:

- BtnA: Select down.
- BtnB: Enter function.
- A+B long press: switch channels.

Sub-function:

- A+B long press: return to the main menu.

M5 TALK：

- BtnA: Start or stop recording.
- BtnB: Send local recordings.
- After receiving the voice pop-up window, BtnB plays it and BtnA confirms and destroys it.

Ordinary message pop-up window:

- BtnA: Confirm and close.

### M5Burner installation

File: `M5_INTEL_v1.0.0_M5Burner_0x0000.bin`

1. Select the custom firmware burning function for M5StickS3 in M5Burner.
2. Select the `.bin` file above.
3. Set the burning address to `0x00000000`.
4. It is recommended to execute Erase Flash before first installation.
5. Select the serial port corresponding to the device and start burning.
6. Both devices must have the same version installed and set to the same channel.

Note: This is a complete merged image that already contains the bootloader, partition table, boot_app0 and application. Do not burn this file to `0x10000`.

### Technical boundaries

- Currently only for communication between M5StickS3 devices.
- Does not connect to Android, iPhone or original Bitchat mobile client.
- M5 TALK is "record and send", not a real-time continuous voice stream.
- Link encryption is not currently enabled for ESP-NOW broadcasts.
- “播放后销毁”表示从运行内存中删除，不等同于经过安全审计的物理数据擦除。\n:
- "Destroy after playing" means deletion from running memory and is not equivalent to physical data erasure after security audit.
- The current ACK logic is mainly aimed at reliable communication scenarios between two devices on the same channel.

Transport: direct ESP-NOW communication between devices on the same channel

1. M5 TALK
   - Records voice with the built-in microphone.
   - Maximum recording length: 8 seconds.

- Currently only for communication between M5StickS3 devices.
- Does not connect to Android, iPhone or original Bitchat mobile client.
- M5 TALK is "record and send", not a real-time continuous voice stream.
- Link encryption is not currently enabled for ESP-NOW broadcasts.
- "Destroy after playing" means deletion from running memory and is not equivalent to physical data erasure after security audit.
- The current ACK logic is mainly aimed at reliable communication scenarios between two devices on the same channel.

---

### Overview

M5 INTEL is an offline, short-range field intelligence firmware for the M5StickS3. Devices communicate directly over ESP-NOW without a phone, computer, Wi-Fi router, or Internet connection. It combines temporary voice messages, preset reports, status codes, numeric intelligence, telemetry, IMU gesture signals, periodic beacons, and SOS alerts in a portrait cyber-terminal interface.

Version: v1.0.0  
Target hardware: M5StickS3 / ESP32-S3-PICO-1 / 8 MB Flash  
Transport: direct ESP-NOW communication between devices on the same channel  
Image type: merged flash image for offset 0x00000000

### Main Features

1. M5 TALK
   - Records voice with the built-in microphone.
   - Maximum recording length: 8 seconds.
   - Displays the live recording duration.
   - Reliably transmits completed recordings to same-channel devices.
   - The receiver shows a global popup with sender identity and duration.
   - BtnB plays the voice message; BtnA confirms and removes it from memory.

2. QUICK INTEL
   - SAFE
   - NEED SUPPORT
   - TARGET FOUND
   - RETREAT
   - RENDEZVOUS
   - MISSION COMPLETE

3. STATUS CODE
   - GREEN
   - AMBER
   - RED
   - HOLD
   - MOVING
   - OFFLINE

4. NUMERIC INTEL
   - Sends numeric intelligence from 00 to 99.
   - Numbers may represent personnel, targets, distance, rooms, or mission IDs.

5. TELEMETRY
   - Sends battery percentage.
   - Sends device uptime.

6. IMU SIGNAL
   - Sends a gesture signal when the device is shaken firmly.
   - Approximate trigger threshold: 2.5g.
   - A 15-second cooldown prevents repeated triggers.
   - Detection is suspended while recording.

7. BEACON
   - Broadcasts presence and battery level every 30 seconds.
   - Operates only when another same-channel device is detected and no recording is active.
   - Runs silently in the background without interrupting the UI.

8. SOS
   - Sends a high-priority emergency alert.
   - The receiver displays a dedicated red SOS screen.
   - A short notification tone is played once.
   - BtnB acknowledges and closes the alert.

### Interface and Message Experience

- Matrix-inspired green digital-rain boot animation.
- Pixel cyber-style M5 INTEL wordmark.
- Black background, green information, and red emergency alerts.
- Portrait interface throughout the firmware.
- Off-screen buffered rendering to reduce visible flicker.
- Current channel and online device count are displayed.
- Voice and intelligence messages can be received from any feature screen.
- Global popups display the complete sender and message, with automatic line wrapping.
- Closing a popup returns the user to the previous screen.
- Periodic beacons stay in the background and do not open popups.

### Reliable Delivery

- Voice is downsampled and split into ESP-NOW fragments.
- Packets include a message ID, fragment index, fragment count, duration, and CRC16.
- The receiver acknowledges every valid fragment.
- The sender selectively retransmits only missing fragments for up to five rounds.
- Quick reports, status codes, numbers, telemetry, IMU signals, and SOS messages also wait for receiver acknowledgement.
- DELIVERED means the receiver confirmed delivery.
- NOT CONFIRMED means complete confirmation was not received and the user should retry.
- Duplicate messages are filtered and incomplete voice assemblies expire automatically.

### Controls

Main menu:

- BtnA: move down.
- BtnB: enter the selected feature.
- Hold A+B: change the ESP-NOW channel.

Inside a feature:

- Hold A+B: return to the main menu.

M5 TALK:

- BtnA: start or stop recording.
- BtnB: send the local recording.
- In an incoming voice popup, BtnB plays and BtnA confirms and destroys the message.

Standard message popup:

- BtnA: acknowledge and close.

File: `M5_INTEL_v1.0.0_M5Burner_0x0000.bin`

1. Open the custom firmware flashing workflow for M5StickS3 in M5Burner.
2. Select the `.bin` file above.
3. Set the flash offset to `0x00000000`.
4. Erase Flash is recommended before the first installation.
5. Select the correct serial port and start flashing.
6. Both devices must run the same firmware version and use the same channel.

Important: this is a complete merged image containing the bootloader, partition table, boot_app0, and application. Do not flash this file at `0x10000`.

## What's this
Turn M5Stack StopWatch into an electronic business card that hangs on your chest. Wear it at exhibitions, events, and technical exchanges: others will know who you are at a glance, and if they want to add you, they can just scan the QR code.

## What can be seen on the screen?
- **Business Card Page**: avatar, name, position and company, several tags; the top shows the time, battery and approximate remaining life.
- **Scan code page**: Large QR code, the brightness is automatically adjusted to the highest level, making it easier for others to scan.
- **Standby page**: It will automatically dim after a period of inactivity and only display the time and name, saving more power.

## How to use the buttons
| Operation | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Short press the yellow key | Open the QR code (full brightness), and automatically return to the business card when the time is up, or press it again to return |
| Short press the blue key | Switch to the next one when there are multiple QR codes; return to the business card when there is only one |
| Press and hold blue key for 2 seconds | Enter/exit "Modify with mobile phone" mode |
| Press any key in standby | Return to business card; press the yellow key to directly open the QR code |
| Power button once / double press | Power on / off |

## Use your mobile phone to change it to your own business card
1. When you turn on the phone for the first time (or press and hold the blue button for 2 seconds), a Wi‑Fi QR code and password will be displayed on the screen.
2. Use the camera that comes with your phone to scan the QR code and connect it to the hotspot on the badge (scanning via WeChat will not work). The phone will automatically open the editing page; if it does not pop up, use a browser to open 192.168.4.1.
3. Fill in the name, position, company, tags, change the avatar, add up to 3 QR codes (you can directly select WeChat QR code screenshots for automatic recognition), and then select the theme and brightness.
4. Click "Publish to Badge" and you're done when you see "Saved". The hotspot will turn off automatically. The entire process does not require an Internet connection, and the information is only saved in the badge.

## Battery Tips
- The "x.xh" next to the battery icon indicates how many hours it can be used and is not displayed when charging.
- When fully charged, it can be used for about 8-9 hours when parked on the business card page; frequently flashing QR codes and turning on hotspots will consume more power.
- It is recommended to fully charge the battery for the first time and then use it until it is almost empty. The badge will remember the actual condition of the battery and the remaining time will be more accurate.
- Press the power button twice to turn off the phone. Time will continue to run after the phone is turned off.

# MAKER FIGHTER

**The hand you make becomes a fist. **

A 1v1 3D fighting game powered by M5Stack Tab5. The fighters, drawn with flat-shaded polygons reminiscent of 90s arcades, are not fighters but makers and engineers. Use the virtual stick on the screen and the three buttons G, P, and K to fight by hitting upper, middle, and lower strikes.

Official website: https://maker-fighter.com/

## Features

- Tab5's software 3D rendering runs at 30fps.
- 1P vs. CPU winner.
- 3 rounds (best 2), time limit 45 seconds, ring out.
- 8 special techniques that can be issued using commands.


## How to play

1. When you turn on the power, the title screen (demo battle between CPUs) will appear. Tap the screen to proceed to character selection.
2. Select a character by tapping the face lined up below, then tap the same face again to confirm (it will be determined automatically after 15 seconds). The first opponent is determined by a roulette wheel.
3. If you win, move on to the next opponent. Even if you lose, you can continue by tapping YES within 10 seconds (no limit to the number of times).

The volume can be changed using the ⚙ button (settings screen) at the top right of the title screen (0 to 10 levels. Saved on the main unit).

You can also play with a USB joystick. Plug directly into the Tab5's USB-A port (USB encoder for Akecom, Xbox 360 compatible pad, PS4 / PS5
pads, etc.). While connected, the pad on the screen will disappear. Button assignments can be changed on the ⚙ settings screen.

## operate

"Front" and "back" are based on the direction of the opponent (the character always faces the opponent).

| Input | Operation |
|---|---|
| Before / After | Walk. Dash before, before / after, after / back dash |
| Bottom | Crouch (does not hit the top row) |
| Top | Jump (short press for a small jump, long press for a large jump) |
| P/K in the air | Jump attack (techniques change while ascending and descending) |
| G | Standing guard (prevents upper and middle attacks) |
| Down + G | Crouching guard (prevents lower step) |
| P | パンチ（上段。P,P,P で 3 連） |\n| 前 + P | 肘:
| P | Punch (upper row. 3 in a row with P, P, P) |
| Front + P | Elbow (midsection) |
| Down + P | Lower punch |
| K | High kick (upper stage) |
| Back + K | Middle kick |
| Down + K | Low kick (lower) |
| Front down + K | Knee (middle. If you hit it, the opponent will float) |
| Forward + K | Big kick (upper stage. Opponent will fall if hit) |
| P + G | Throw (at close range. Can also be used by opponents who are standing guard) |
| Down + P / Up + P | Stomp / Diving Elbow |
| While falling down, press G or up / behind / K | Get up on the spot / Roll backwards / Kick to get up |

- Crouch to dodge the upper stage. The middle stage cannot be blocked by crouching guard, and the bottom stage cannot be blocked by standing guard.
- Counter (1.5x damage) if you hit the opponent while they are using a technique.
- Special skill commands (→↘P, ↓→P, ←Charge→P, K+P+G, etc.) can be viewed along with the moves on the MOVE LIST of CHARACTER on the official website.

- M5Stack Tab5
- (optional) USB joystick

- 3 rounds (best 2), time limit 45 seconds, ring out.
- 8 special techniques that can be issued using commands.


## How to play

1. When you turn on the power, the title screen (demo battle between CPUs) will appear. Tap the screen to proceed to character selection.
2. Select a character by tapping the face lined up below, then tap the same face again to confirm (it will be determined automatically after 15 seconds). The first opponent is determined by a roulette wheel.
3. If you win, move on to the next opponent. Even if you lose, you can continue by tapping YES within 10 seconds (no limit to the number of times).

The volume can be changed using the ⚙ button (settings screen) at the top right of the title screen (0 to 10 levels. Saved on the main unit).

You can also play with a USB joystick. Plug directly into the Tab5's USB-A port (USB encoder for Akecom, Xbox 360 compatible pad, PS4 / PS5
pads, etc.). While connected, the pad on the screen will disappear. Button assignments can be changed on the ⚙ settings screen.

## operate

"Front" and "back" are based on the direction of the opponent (the character always faces the opponent).

| Input | Operation |
|---|---|
| Before / After | Walk. Dash before, before / after, after / back dash |
| Bottom | Crouch (does not hit the top row) |
| Top | Jump (short press for a small jump, long press for a large jump) |
| P/K in the air | Jump attack (techniques change while ascending and descending) |
| G | Standing guard (prevents upper and middle attacks) |
| Down + G | Crouching guard (prevents lower step) |
| P | Punch (upper row. 3 in a row with P, P, P) |
| Front + P | Elbow (midsection) |
| Down + P | Lower punch |
| K | High kick (upper stage) |
| Back + K | Middle kick |
| Down + K | Low kick (lower) |
| Front down + K | Knee (middle. If you hit it, the opponent will float) |
| Forward + K | Big kick (upper stage. Opponent will fall if hit) |
| P + G | Throw (at close range. Can also be used by opponents who are standing guard) |
| Down + P / Up + P | Stomp / Diving Elbow |
| While falling down, press G or up / behind / K | Get up on the spot / Roll backwards / Kick to get up |

- Crouch to dodge the upper stage. The middle stage cannot be blocked by crouching guard, and the bottom stage cannot be blocked by standing guard.
- Counter (1.5x damage) if you hit the opponent while they are using a technique.
- Special skill commands (→↘P, ↓→P, ←Charge→P, K+P+G, etc.) can be viewed along with the moves on the MOVE LIST of CHARACTER on the official website.

- M5Stack Tab5
- (optional) USB joystick

- Native support for M5Stack PaperMono
- E-Ink refresh strategy optimized for SSD1677
- Smoother menu and firmware browsing interaction
-Support touch/button/SD card/front light
- Firmware checking and protected payload installation
- Payload startup and return to Launcher recovery process
- Support independent ESP32-S3 application firmware installation
- Supports eligible simple single-application FullFlash wrapper firmware (F1-v1)
- Continue to block installation of unsupported multi-partition coupled FullFlash firmware

### Quick use

After burning is completed:

1. Start PaperMono.
2. Enter Launcher in the launch selection interface.
3. Use touch or side buttons to perform menu operations.
4. Enter the SD/firmware browser to view the firmware file.
5. Only firmware that passes the compatibility and security checks will display the Install option.
6. After launching the installed payload, you can re-enter the Launcher through the supported return/recovery process.


### Firmware Compatibility

PaperMono Launcher does not consider all `.bin` files as firmware that is safe to install.

Launcher will only extract and install FullFlash packaged firmware that qualifies for F1-v1

| Swipe down from the top edge of the screen | Open the front light panel. |
| Click the bookmark control | to add or remove bookmarks for the current page. |
| Swipe up from the bottom edge of the screen | Return to the library. |

The reading settings panel allows you to adjust font size, line spacing, and open the table of contents and bookmark list. When using the TF card for the first time, PaperMono may install built-in Chinese fonts; please keep the TF card inserted until the startup is completed.

### 4. Device settings

Click `SET` in the launcher.

#### Brightness

Drag the brightness slider, or click the `-`, `+` buttons to adjust in 10% increments. The percentage shown on the right is the saved brightness value.

#### sound

Click the `SOUND` row or the switch on the right to turn global sound preferences on or off. It affects the local sound reminder; the Mesh message reminder method needs to be selected separately in the Mesh settings.

#### Firmware version

The `FIRMWARE` line displays the `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS` Build ID of the currently installed firmware. Please provide this number when reporting a problem or confirming whether the new firmware has been burned.

### 5. Basic use of Mesh

Click `MESH` in the launcher. Mesh pages have independent bottom navigation:

| Tags | Features |
| --- | --- |
| `OVR` | Overview of native node, radio and device metrics. |
| `INBOX` | Conversation list and message editor. |
| `NODES` | Known nodes and private message entry. |
| `SET` | Radio, alerts, lights and local data settings. |

#### Select radio area

Before using LoRa, please enter `OVR` and click on the status area to select the applicable area configuration. Only use radio zones and emission parameters that are permitted for your location.

#### Connect to Meshtastic Mobile App

1. Turn on your phone’s Bluetooth.
2. Select the PaperMono device in the Meshtastic App.
3. Follow the steps in the App to complete pairing. If PaperMono displays a pairing code, please enter or confirm the code in the app.
4. Keep the app open until the first configuration and node data synchronization are completed.

The device will continue to serve Mesh based on the Mesh background running settings. Bluetooth, phone sync, and radio activity may take a short time to resume after powering on or reconnecting.

### 6. Messages and Conversations

1. Click on `INBOX`.
2. Click a conversation to enter the conversation page.
3. 点击 `TAP TO WRITE A MESSAGE` 打开屏幕键盘。\n:
3. Click `TAP TO WRITE A MESSAGE` to open the on-screen keyboard.
4. Enter the text and send.

On the session page, click `INBOX` in the Mesh navigation at the bottom to return to the session list. An unread logo may appear below the `INBOX` label. A message sent by this machine will display the delivery status: `SENT` only means that the local radio has accepted the delivery; subsequent confirmation may update the status to `DELIVERED` or `FAILED`.

### 7. Nodes and private messages

Click `NODES` to view discovered nodes. The title area displays total, online and offline statistics. Clicking on a remote node row opens the private message editor for that node.

Node discovery and message delivery depend on locale, modem preset, channel configuration, antenna, distance, and intermediate mesh nodes. Just because a node is displayed on the screen does not mean that end-to-end delivery can be completed immediately.

### 8. Mesh settings

Go to `MESH` > `SET`. Click the corresponding item to switch or open the settings.

| Settings | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| `MESH BACKGROUND` | Whether to continue serving the Mesh runtime when using other PaperMono applications. |
| `MODEM PRESET` | Switch LoRa modem preset; needs to be compatible with the target Mesh. |
| `HOP LIMIT` | Switch the maximum number of routing hops. |
| `TX POWER` | Toggle transmit power setting; please comply with local radio regulations. |
| `MESSAGE ALERTS` | Switch message reminders between off, sound, light, sound + light. |
| `LIGHT STYLE` | Select the unread message light reminder style supported by the device. |
| `DATA & HISTORY` | View and clear saved messages and/or node caches. |

Cleanup operations in `DATA & HISTORY` are irreversible. Clearing the node cache will also remove the saved node name and private message public key information, and you will need to resynchronize the private message key afterwards.

### 9. Shut down

Double-clicking the side power button will initiate a controlled shutdown process. Please wait until the shutdown screen is completed before disconnecting the power or storing the device. A short press may only be responded to by the power management hardware and is not a normal software shutdown operation.

### 10. Precautions when using the ink screen

-Avoid direct sunlight, high temperatures and strong UV rays.
- Do not continue to perform high-frequency interface operations for a long time.
- The firmware will merge rapid refreshes of the same area and perform clean refreshes after a certain number of times; these are protective measures and are not a substitute for careful use.
- 正常使用后若出现持续残影，请等待界面进行下一次全屏刷新；避免反复强制快速变化:
- If persistent image persistence occurs after normal use, please wait for the next full-screen refresh of the interface; avoid repeated forced rapid changes.

### 11. FAQ

| Phenomenon | Possible solutions |
| --- | --- |
| New books are not displayed | Confirm that the TF card is inserted and the file is EPUB, then reopen `LIB`. |
| Mesh No Activity | Verify that the zone settings are correct, the channel/modulation settings match, the antenna connections are working, and there are reachable nodes nearby. |
| The phone cannot connect | Turn off and on the phone's Bluetooth, reconnect in the Meshtastic App, and complete the pairing code process displayed on the device. |
| Private message failed after clearing data | Waiting for node information to be resynchronized; clearing the node cache will remove the saved private message key material. |
| There is an obvious afterimage on the screen | Stop quick operations and wait for full-screen refresh, and avoid high temperature and direct sunlight. |

If you need to report firmware issues, please provide the Build ID, specific device model and related serial port logs in `SET` > `FIRMWARE`.

## Build/Write

```bash
# build
pio run

# Write firmware (with the actual device connected via USB)
pio run -t upload

# Write the audio clip (data/voice/*.pcm) to LittleFS (execute for the first time/when changing the clip)
pio run -t uploadfs

# serial monitor
pio device monitor
```

During the first build, `M5.getBoard()` reports `board_M5StopWatch` in the serial log.
Please make sure to return it (if it is different, it may be due to hardware such as PSRAM not detected).
possible).

## About audio reading clips

`data/voice/*.pcm` is a 16bit / 16kHz / monaural pre-recorded audio clip,
`alert_engine.cpp` displays call signs, etc., one clip per alphabet/number
This is a connected playback method (free text park names and mountain names are not read out).

The clips currently included are the macOS standard `say` command (English audio).
Samantha). The quality is not a problem in practical use, but it is more natural.
If you want to make audio, use the same file name (26 types of NATO phonetics + numbers 0-9 +
pota/sota/qrt) and replace it with 16bit/16kHz/monaural PCM (no header) audio.
Please rerun `pio run -t uploadfs`.

## Current scope (initial release)
- アラート: CWトーン / 音声読み上げ(録音クリップ)。CWバイブ(振動):
- Alert: CW tone / voice reading (recorded clip). CW vibe (vibration) is not supported.
- Filter only has a single global setting (multiple named presets on Android version are not supported).
There is no list editing UI for bands/modes etc. on the main body, but ON/OFF and numerical parameters.
You can adjust the settings on the main unit settings screen.
- Exclusion by Hunted/Chased (CSV import) is not supported.
- Notified/acknowledged state is RAM-retained only and is lost on reboot
(Immediately after restarting, the alert may sound again for the currently matched spot).
- Bluetooth related functions are not supported (the main unit is WiFi only).

# Literacy · Pinyin — M5Paper Children’s Ink Screen Learning Cards

> **Made by Tim** · v0.1.5
> E-ink screen eye protection study companion: no backlight, deep sleep power saving, progress memory

![cover](screenshots/cover.png)

## Function

| Module | Content |
|---|---|
| **Literacy** | First Grade Volume 1 **100 Chinese Characters** (Full Volume of Ministry-Compiled Writing Lists) · Recognize → Write → Use Cognitive Closed Loop |
| | Recognition: complete word + pinyin + word combination (2 two-character words + 1 four-character word) + sentence making (target word highlighted) |
| | Write: **M character grid stroke by stroke demonstration** (current pen is solid / has written gray lining / has not written outline) + stroke name + stroke order column |
| **Pinyin** | **63 items**: initial consonants 23 · finals 24 · overall reading 16 |
| | Four lines and three frames (letter baseline anchoring) · Pronunciation formula · Example words · Finals/overall recognition and reading **Four-tone tone-by-tone demonstration** |
| **Home** | Big Clock + Date + Dual Entry Card |
| **Time synchronization** | Tap the clock area → Wi-Fi connection + SNTP network time synchronization (direct to the distribution network when not configured) |
| **Settings** | Gear in the upper right corner → Wi-Fi scan configuration (touch the PIN pad)/Set the time immediately/About |
| **Power Saving** | Automatically sleep deeply after 5 minutes of idle time (ink screen saver, side button to wake up to continue learning) |

![home](screenshots/home.png)
![cards](screenshots/card_hanzi.png)
![pinyin](screenshots/card_pinyin.png)

## Install

### Method 1: M5Burner (recommended)

1. Open M5Burner → Device selection **M5Paper**
2. Enter User Firmware/Publish Firmware and point to this warehouse (including `m5burner.json`)
3. One-click burning (including all data partitions, about 11MB)

### Method 2: Manual burning with esptool

```bash
# Replace PORT with your serial port (macOS: /dev/cu.usbserial-*, Windows: COMx)
PORT=/dev/cu.usbserial-XXXXX
esptool.py --chip esp32 -p $PORT -b 460800 write_flash \
0x1000 firmware/bootloader_0x1000.b:
0x1000    firmware/bootloader_0x1000.bin \
  0x8000    firmware/partitions_0x8000.bin \
  0x10000   firmware/shizi_card_0x10000.bin \
  0x310000  firmware/shizi_0x310000.bin \
  0xb80000  firmware/pinyin_0xb80000.bin
```

> The file name is the burning address (`name_address.bin`), and all five files are indispensable.

## use

| Operation | Action |
|---|---|
| Tap the left card / right card on the homepage | Enter literacy / pinyin |
| Tap the clock area on the home page | Network time synchronization |
| Gear in the upper right corner of the homepage | Settings (Network Distribution/Time Synchronization/About) |
| Tap the screen during literacy | Step by step demonstration (left 1/3 = review of the previous stroke) |
| Short press of left/right key | Previous item/Next item |
| Short press of the middle button | Replay |
| Long press the left button for 1.5s | Screen rotation direction (memory) |
| Long press the middle button for 2s | Deep sleep |
| Press and hold the right button for 1.5s during literacy | Return to home page |

## Hardware/Technology

- **M5Paper** (ESP32-D0WD · 960×540 e-ink screen IT8951 · GT911 touch · 16MB Flash)
- ESP-IDF v5.5.1 + M5GFX
- Content pipeline: makemeahanzi stroke data + standardized stroke order table + italic font → full pre-baked bitmap
- The first cognitive design: recognize the sound and shape of characters → follow the kinesthetic sense of writing → use group words to make sentences

## Version

| Version | Description |
|---|---|
| 0.1.5 | First public release: Literacy 100 words + Pinyin 63 items + Wi-Fi time synchronization + settings |

# 🪇 Детская погремушка — M5StickC Plus2\:
# 🪇 Baby rattle – M5StickC Plus2

You shake it and it plays and lights up. Three modes, safe volume and brightness, can fall asleep on its own if you forget about it.

## What is this

The regular M5StickC Plus2 is turned into a musical toy for kids: hand movement gives a note and color on the screen. No wires or apps - turn it on and you can play. The volume and brightness are programmatically limited specifically for children's ears and eyes, and if the device is left lying idle, it will dim itself and fall asleep, saving the battery.

## Turn on and off

At the end of the device there is a power button. Pressing turns on the screen, long holding turns the device off completely.

While the device is turned on, it can fall asleep on its own (see [“Sleep”](#sleep) below) - you don’t need to press anything separately to do this.

## Modes

There are three modes, switched with the **A** button in a circle: Rattle → Box → Piano → Rattle.

### 🪇 Rattle
Самый простой режим. Трясёшь — звучит но:
The easiest mode. When you shake it, a note sounds and the screen flashes color. The harder you shake, the brighter the screen “breathes.”

### 🎵 Box

You need to shake it several times to “start it up” - then the melody plays itself, and the color on the screen slowly shimmers. As the plant runs out, the music slows down - shake again to continue.

### 🎹 Piano

You tilt the device and the pitch of the note changes in steps, like keys. The sound comes only while you move: stopped - silence, although the bar on the screen will remain showing the last note.

## Management

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| **A** (under screen) | Switch mode. If the device is asleep, the first press wakes it up and does not change the mode; you need to press again. |
| **B** (side) | Switch the volume in a circle: Quiet → Normal → Silent → Quiet. |

## Screen
В верхней полоске — название текущего ре:
The top bar contains the name of the current mode, the volume icon and the battery charge indicator. When charging via USB-C, a lightning bolt appears next to the battery. The less charge, the more alarming the color of the indicator (yellow, then red).

## Dream

If the device lies motionless for about 20 seconds, the screen dims. After about another minute, it goes out and the device falls asleep completely, almost without wasting the battery. You can wake up by shaking or pressing **A** - the mode and volume are not lost. While the device is connected to USB, it does not fall asleep on its own—it’s convenient if it just lies on the table while charging.

## If something went wrong

- **“IMU” lights up red on the strip**—the motion sensor is not detected. This is not a malfunction in the usual sense: pressing **A** will still play a note and flash on the screen, the **B** button will still change the volume, but switching between the three modes is not available until the sensor is working.
- **Экран мигнул сообщением «Заряд» и ус:
- **The screen flashed the message “Charging” and the device turned off** - the battery was almost completely discharged, this is normal behavior to protect the battery. Just charge via USB-C.


## For those who want to look under the hood

The firmware is compiled via [PlatformIO](https://platformio.org/) (`pio run -e m5stack-stickc-plus2`), built on [M5Unified](https://github.com/m5stack/M5Unified).

# Tetris for M5Stack Faces Gamepad3

## Introduction

A lightweight Tetris game designed for M5Stack CoreS3 series devices. It is developed based on ESP-IDF and GameLib and needs to be used with Faces Bottom3 and Faces Gamepad3.

### Game Features

- Classic 10 × 20 block matrix
- 7 standard blocks
- Block rotation and wall correction
- Ghost block preview
- Hold temporary storage function
- Continuous elimination and level system
- Highest score record
- Pause, resume and restart
- Adapted to Faces Bottom3 and Faces Gamepad3

### How to operate

- Left click/right click: move the block
- Down key: rapid descent
- Up key: drop directly to the bottom
- A key: rotate clockwise
- B key: rotate counterclockwise
- START: Temporarily save the current block
- SELECT: Pause the game
- Press the up/down keys during pause: choose to continue or restart
- Press B in the pause interface: confirm the selection
- Press SELECT while paused: continue the game
- Press B when the game is over: restart

### Hardware requirements

- M5Stack CoreS3 或 CoreS3-Lite
- Faces Bottom3
- Faces Gamepad3

## First time use

1. Press **T** on the homepage to set the date and time, press **S** to enter the settings and fill in the **birthday**.
2. Cardputer does not have a clock that is maintained when powered off: When not in use, please **press and hold G0 to enter standby** and do not turn the switch to power off. The clock continues to run during standby, press any key or G0 to wake up.
3. After a real power outage, a "Time to be calibrated" prompt will appear on the homepage, press **T** to calibrate; if WiFi is filled in, it will automatically connect to the Internet to calibrate the time after a power outage (it will not connect to the Internet when waking up from standby).
4. Recording and Pomodoro statistics require an SD card in **FAT32** format.

## General keys

- **Direction keys**: `;` (up), `.` (down), `,` (left), `/` (right) on the keyboard. While entering text, you need to hold down **Fn** and then press it.
- **Esc**: `` `` `` key in the upper left corner. **Esc** or **Backspace (Del)** can return to the homepage from any page.
- **Enter** to confirm, **Space** to start or execute.
- When the screen is off, pressing it for the first time will only light up the screen and will not trigger operations (except page turner pages).

## Global shortcut keys (valid on any page)

- **Short press G0** or **Ctrl+R**: Start recording with one click, press again to stop
- **Press and hold G0 for about 1.5 seconds**: enter standby (a circle of progress appears in the middle of the screen, and when it is full, it is standby); press any key or G0 to wake up; cannot standby during Pomodoro timer
- **Fn+1 / Fn+2 / Fn+3**: Start recording directly with the corresponding preset (random recording / long-term recording / high-fidelity 44.1kHz)

## Home · The rest of your life

- Arrow keys, Enter, Tab or Space: open the bottom app bar; ←→ (or Tab) switches, Enter or Space opens, Esc closes
- Direct access to the letter keys: **L** Xiao Liuren **Q** Asking for lots **J** Throwing dice **D** Dice **C** Coin **R** Recording **F** Recording library **P** Pomodoro **K** Page turner **S** Settings
- Numbers **1–9**: Open directly in the order of the app bar
- **U**：进入 U 盘模式\n- **T**：校准时间（←→ 选择年 /:
- **U**: Enter U disk mode
- **T**: Calibration time (←→ select year/month/day/hour/minute, ↑↓ to adjust, hold down Shift once 10, you can also enter numbers directly; Enter to confirm, **W** to online time calibration, Esc to cancel)

## Xiao Liuren

- **Space**: Time to start class (automatically takes the current lunar month, day, and time)
- **Tab**: Switch between "Time to start class/Time to start class"
- Start the lesson by reporting numbers: After entering the number, press space to confirm. Enter three numbers in total; **Backspace key** deletes one digit, and returns to the previous number if there is no digit to be deleted.
- After the results are displayed, press **Enter** to see the vertical poem, and then press Enter or Esc to return.
- Within the same hour, the result of starting class at that hour remains unchanged (traditional algorithm)

## Asking for lots / throwing dice / dice / coins

- **Hold the space (or Enter) to charge, then release to throw**. The fuller the charge, the harder the throw; tap once to throw lightly.
- You can also directly **swing the device** to draw or throw
- Requesting a signature: After signing, press **Enter** to see detailed explanations (career, wealth, relationship, health, travel), and then press Enter to return to the signature; **J** then throw the fork to ask for instructions; **Space** to request a signature again
- Toss: Holy Grail (one flat and one convex), Laughing Cup (two flat), Yin Cup (two convex); winning the Holy Cup three times in a row has special effects
- Dice: **1–6** Select the number of dice, or use **- / =** to increase or decrease
- Coin: **C** or **0** clear heads and tails count

## Recording

- **↑↓** or **1–3** Select preset, **Enter** or space to start recording
- Recording: **Space** to pause or continue, **M** to mark, **Enter** to stop and save
- Pressing Esc to return to the homepage during recording will not interrupt the recording: the recording duration will be displayed on the homepage, and there will be a red dot in the upper right corner of other pages.
- The screen automatically dims and turns off during recording to save power (can be adjusted in settings); press any key to light up
- **F**: Open the recording library
- The file is saved in SD card `/REC/` and named according to the recording time; long-term recording will be automatically continued in segments

## Recording library

- **↑↓** Select, **Enter** or space to play
- **D**: Delete (click twice to confirm, a red prompt will appear when you press the first time)
- **R**: Start a new recording, **U**: Enter U disk mode
- 播放中：**空格 / Enter** 暂停或继续；**←→** 快退或快进:
- Playing: **Space / Enter** to pause or continue; **←→** to rewind or forward 5 seconds, hold **Shift** once for 30 seconds; **- / =** volume; **N / P** to jump to the next or previous mark; **Esc** to return to the list

## Pomodoro

- List: **↑↓** selection, **Enter** or space start
- **E** edit the current preset, **N** create new (you can also select the last line "+ New"), **D** delete (click twice to confirm)
- **Tab**: View statistics (today’s minutes, number of tomatoes, consecutive days, last 7 days), and then press Tab or Esc to return
- Edit: **↑↓** select the field, **←→** adjust the value (hold Shift once ±5), press **Enter** on "Name" to enter the name (English supported), Enter or Esc to save
- Timing: **Space/Enter** to pause or continue, **S** to skip the current stage, **X** (or backspace key) to press twice to end
- Press Esc to return to the home page during timing. The timing will continue in the background and the progress will be displayed on the home page.
- Rest will automatically start when concentration is over; after the rest, press space to start the next round, and turn on "Pomodoro Automatic Start" in the settings to start automatically
- Focus records are saved in SD card `/POMO/focus.csv`

## Kindle page turner (experimental)

- First time pairing: Open "Settings › Bluetooth Devices" on Kindle and select **TianJi Click**
- **→ ↓ Space Enter N**: Next page **← ↑ B**: Previous page
- **- / =**: Kindle brightness
- **Z**: Put Kindle to sleep
- **F**: Clear pairing (click twice to confirm, also "forget device" on Kindle)
- When reading a book, the screen will automatically turn off after 20 seconds. You can still turn pages by pressing the buttons when the screen is off.
- Bluetooth is only turned on in this page and will be turned off automatically after leaving; it is not available during recording
- Not yet verified on a real Kindle, feedback is welcome

## USB disk mode

- When plugged into the computer, a 3-second countdown will pop up. Press any key to cancel; after the countdown is over, the SD card will appear on the computer as a USB flash drive.
- Eject the USB flash drive or unplug the data cable from the computer, and the device will automatically return to normal mode
- To exit manually: Double-click **Esc**
- You can also press **U** on the homepage or enter manually in the settings; "Automatic U disk plug-in" can be turned off in the settings

## set up
- **↑↓** 选择，**←→** 调整数值或开关，**Enter** 编辑文:
- **↑↓** select, **←→** adjust values ​​or switches, **Enter** edit text items
- When editing text: Direct input, **Backspace** to delete, **Enter** to confirm, **Fn+`** to cancel
- Press Enter in "Date Time" to open the time calibration interface (the operation is the same as T on the home page)
- Configurable: birthday, life expectancy, date and time, WiFi, automatic time adjustment (off/after power off/every day), WiFi off after time adjustment, time zone, brightness, volume, sound effects, recording sampling rate, recording gain, recording dimming and screen off, focus screen off, Pomodoro automatic start, Bluetooth page turner switch, plug in automatic USB flash drive, enter standby
- After closing the "Bluetooth Page Turner", it will restart once, releasing the memory reserved by Bluetooth for other functions, and saving more power.

# Wifi_RIG_CTRL for M5Stack Core2  Ver 2.20

This firmware makes M5Stack Core2 a remote controller for radio equipment (rig).
Operate your rig via Raspberry Pi (Wifi_Rig_CTRL FastAPI backend) or ICOM WLAN Remote (CI-V over WiFi),
Supports APRS beacon transmission and PTT control via Wifi_Rig_PTT (relay board sold separately)/Hamlib.

by JI1ORE

---

## 1. Included files

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/` `include/` `platformio.ini` `merge_bin.py` | Source set (PlatformIO project) |
| `M5CoreHamCAT_Core2_v2.20.bin` | Pre-built firmware (merged, can be written to address 0x0) |

If you want to use the written `.bin` directly, write it to address 0x0 using esptool etc.

```bash
esptool.py --chip esp32 write_flash 0x0 M5CoreHamCAT_Core2_v2.20.bin
```

If you want to build it yourself, open this folder as a project in PlatformIO (VSCode extension or CLI) and
Run `Build` / `Upload`.

```bash
pio run # build
pio run -t upload # build + write
```
M5Stack Core2 Tough / M5Stack CoreS3 SE:
M5Stack Core2 Tough / M5Stack CoreS3 SE are published in separate folders (`M5CoreHamCAT_Core2Tough` / `M5CoreHamCAT_CoreS3SE`).

---

## 2. Hardware connection (role of Port)

| Port | Pin | Application |
|---|---|---|
| **Port A** | SDA=G32 / SCL=G33 (+GND/5V) | **Rotary encoder** (Connect M5 genuine I2C encoder unit Unit Encoder / SKU:U135) |
| **Port C** | G13 / G14 (+GND/5V) | **PTT key input (G13) + status LED (G14)**. Details below |

### Port C wiring (important)

- **G13 ⟷ GND**: Connect the PTT contact of an external toggle switch/foot switch/mechanical key (M5 genuine SK6812, etc.) here.
Since G13 has an internal pull-up (`INPUT_PULLUP`), you can simply connect the switch between G13 and Port C's GND (no additional components such as a pull-up resistor are required).
- **G14**: Data input for WS2812 compatible NeoPixel (1 light). Displays the transmission/reception status by LED color (described later).

> **Important specification**: The actual transmission (PTT ON) is only when **the "PTT" button on the screen is ON (`txEnabled`)** and **G13 of Port C is closed (LOW)**.
> Even if you tap only the "PTT" button on the screen, data will not be transmitted if nothing is connected to Port C.
> Assumed operation: This is a two-stage safety design in which transmission is permitted (armed) using the "PTT" button on the screen, and the actual transmission timing is controlled using an external switch (foot switch, etc.).

### Status LED (Port C, G14) color

| Color | Condition |
|---|---|
| Red | **Actually transmitting** (Hamlib / Wifi_Rig_PTT / CI-V any method) |
| 青 | 送信スタンバイ中（画面のPTTボタンON＝アーム済み、PTT方式=W:
| Blue | Transmission standby (PTT button on screen = armed, PTT method = Wifi_Rig_PTT, no actual transmission) |
| Green | Transmission standby (PTT button on screen = armed, PTT method = Hamlib or CI-V) |
| Off | PTT button on screen OFF (transmission arm is released) |

### Screen orientation

Core2 does not rotate the screen (vertically flip it) and displays it in its normal orientation (screen flipping is only available in the Core2 Tough version).

### Audio

In addition to the built-in microphone/speaker, Core2 allows you to select external Module Audio (ES8388, I2C: SDA=G21, SCL=G22).
On the settings screen (PTT Method screen), you can select the SPK output destination and Mic input destination independently from built-in or Module Audio (external) (default is built-in).
If you are not using Module Audio, no external wiring is required.

---

## 3. Flow from initial startup to connection

### 3-1. Startup screen (splash)

When you turn on the power, the "Wifi_Rig_CTRL" logo will be displayed, followed by two buttons: **Normal** / **Skip**.

- **Normal**: Normal startup. Proceed in the following order: Wi-Fi selection → Raspberry Pi/CI-V connection → Rig selection → PTT method selection, checking the settings each time.
- **Skip**: Use the previously saved settings (Wi-Fi, Pi connection destination, rig, PTT method) to skip the confirmation screen and automatically connect to the main screen at once.

At the top left of the screen there is a small toggle labeled **Default:Normal/Default:Skip**. If you tap this and set it to "Default: Skip",
**If you do not tap anything for 8 seconds, the automatic transition destination will be Skip** (If you tap the Normal/Skip button on the spot, that will take priority).
If you want to start with Skip every time, you can set this default value to Skip once, and from then on it will automatically start with Skip without pressing a button.

### 3-2. Wi-Fi connection screen

Scans and displays a list of nearby Wi-Fi (Android tethering, etc.). Tap the SSID and enter the password to connect.
### 3-3. Raspberry Pi / CI-V 接続画面\n\n画面右:
### 3-3. Raspberry Pi / CI-V connection screen

Switch the connection method using **"Pi Mode"/"CI-V"** at the top right of the screen.

- **Pi Mode** (via Raspberry Pi + rigctld/FastAPI backend)
- Hostname (or IP address. mDNS use/non-use can be switched)
  - API Port / Audio Port
- API Key (optional, only if authentication is required on the backend side)
- **CI-V** (ICOM WLAN Remote compatible, directly connected to radio's WiFi. No Pi required)
- Host (IP address of the radio)
- Ctrl Port / CIV Port / Addr(hex) (CI-V address)
- Username / Password (authentication information set on the radio device side)
- Timeout (time until the screen turns off when there is no operation)

After entering the information, tap "Connect".

### 3-4. Rig selection screen

Select the operation target from the rig list obtained from the connection destination (Pi/CI-V).

### 3-5. PTT mode selection screen

- **Wifi_PTT**: A method of sending PTT signals to the separately sold Wifi_Rig_PTT relay (Remotekeyer) via WiFi/UDP. This method was prepared to avoid the problem of not being able to modulate when using PTT via Hamlib on an ICOM machine.
- Set PTT Host (mDNS name or IP address) and PTT Port
- **Hamlib**: A method of performing normal CAT PTT control via rigctld.
- Set PTT Device (serial device) and PTT Type (RTS/DTR)

After setting, click "OK" to move to the main screen.

---

## 4. How to operate the main screen

### Upper row (Status display)

- Left: Connected model name
- Top right tip (from left):
1. **Theme tip** (e.g. "OCN"): Tap to switch design theme in the order of **OCN → AMB → MONO**
2. **昼夜チップ**（\"NGT\"/\"DAY\"）：タップで夜間⇄日:
2. **Day/Night Chip** ("NGT"/"DAY"): Switch from night to day display with a tap.
